patch.value: GH-1032: extension manifests silently accept unenforced version-floor spellings
Extension compatibility tooling ignores unknown or naturally misplaced manifest keys, allowing packages to declare apparent pm version floors that no runtime or author-time check reads.

Define the authoritative manifest key schema in the SDK; detect unknown top-level and compatibility-like nested keys without rejecting legitimate extension namespaces; add typed findings and exact migration targets; apply the same analyzer to scaffolding, package doctor, CLI, MCP, contracts, and first-party package governance; test the three reported spellings plus negative controls in disposable packages; document compatibility and rollout behavior.
Make extension compatibility declarations schema-closed and impossible to mistake for enforced policy.
Package authors receive deterministic diagnostics for misspelled, misplaced, stale, or unsupported compatibility declarations.
Packages can remain green while shipping a version floor that no consumer enforces, causing fleet drift and downstream history incompatibility.
SDK analyzers, manifests, scaffolds, package doctor, CLI, MCP, and contracts share one strict compatibility-key vocabulary with migration guidance.
GitHub #1032 documents three live packages with three spellings and silent green checks.
Current extension manifest SDK and package fleet on 2026-08-15

Pass manifests containing compatibility.pm, nested pm.pm_min_version, and stale top-level pm_min_version through checkExtensionManifestCompatibility; observe no unknown-key finding and compatible=true for the first two.
Unknown or misplaced compatibility-like keys are diagnosed with a stable typed finding and an executable correction; valid top-level pm_min_version remains enforced across SDK and package surfaces.
Compatibility-looking fields can be ignored silently, so internally consistent packages and tests remain green while no version floor is enforced.
